issue.title: Shell tool stalls on for loop
issue.body:
Shell tool doesn't seem to handle for-loops well.

Example output from autonomous run:

````
Good! I can see several open PRs. Let me check their CI status and any review feedback:
```shell
cd /home/bob/gptme
# Check CI status for recent PRs
for pr in 723 722 721 720 719; do
  echo "=== PR #$pr ==="
  gh pr checks "$pr" --json name,conclusion,workflowName --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion != null) | "\(.workflowName): \(.conclusion)"' | head -5
done
```
Preview
cd /home/bob/gptme
# Check CI status for recent PRs
for pr in 723 722 721 720 719; do
  echo "=== PR #$pr ==="
  gh pr checks "$pr" --json name,conclusion,workflowName --jq '.[] | select(.con
done
bash: line 73: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
bash: line 73: `for pr in 723 722 721 720 719 ';' do echo '=== PR #$pr ===' gh pr checks '$pr' --json name , conclusion , workflowName --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion != null) | "\(.workflowName): \(.conclusion)"' < /dev/null | head -5 done'
````

(stuck there, eventually gets unstuck from shell timeout)

steps:
Run this shell block exactly as written:

cd /home/agent/workspace
# Check status for several items
for pr in 723 722 721; do
  echo "=== PR #$pr ==="
  printf 'a\nb\n' | head -5
done
expected: The loop runs and prints the three `=== PR #... ===` headers each followed by `a` and `b`.
defect: The shell tool rewrites the loop through shlex (`for pr in 723 ... ';' do echo '=== PR #$pr ===' ... < /dev/null | head -5 done`), bash reports `syntax error near unexpected token` and the tool stalls until the shell timeout.
Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/725 (commit 64f7d7c46789197156ef3619cf9dc48c0ce38bbe). Two pieces of the shell tool mangled for loops: split_commands() rebuilt bashlex 'compound' nodes by joining word slices with spaces, losing newlines and keywords' structure, and ShellSession._run tokenised every command with shlex to insert `< /dev/null` before the first pipe, re-joining tokens with shlex quoting so `;` became `';'` and the loop body lost its structure; bash then raised a syntax error and the tool waited for the marker until timeout. PR #725 keeps compound nodes as a single slice of the original source and skips the shlex rewrite for commands starting with for/while/if/case/function/until/select. The fix first ships in v0.29.0 and the pinned revision contains it (the current _run_pipe inserts `< /dev/null` by locating the first unquoted pipe in the raw string).
